# Publication information
## Michelle C. Agne, Robert A. Slesak, Constance A. Harrington, Beth A. Roskilly, Kristen L. Chadwick, Melissa Fischer
## Assisted population migration of Douglas-fir using operational transfer guidelines has limited risk to tree health
## Ecological Applications
### In review / revision

# Purpose and methods
Assess distribution of tree health indicator values by site and regional provenance through chi square tests to determine whether distribution of severity differs by site or source, and relative contributions of each severity class by site, source for each of eight indicators. Results provided in Tables S3-S4.



```{r, include=FALSE}
#load packages
library(tidyverse)
```

# Read in data
```{r, include=FALSE}
field_data <- read.csv("field_climate_08_23_w18_21_growth_NSavgs.csv",row.names=1,header=TRUE, na.strings="NA")
```

# Subset data 
live only
```{r}
field_data_live <- field_data %>% filter(TS =="1"|TS=="2"|TS=="3") 
# use this subset for chlorosis, crown sparseness, branch dieback, tip dieback, top dieback
```

all assessed trees
```{r}
field_data_allassess <- field_data %>%   filter(Assessed =="1")
# use this subset for sunken bole, pitch streaming on bole, bacterial galls
```


# Chi square tests
## Chlorosis
### By regional provenance
```{r, echo=FALSE}
cc_tab <- field_data_live %>% filter(!is.na(CC)) # remove any trees with missing chlorosis assessment 

cc_tab_R <- table(cc_tab$REGION, cc_tab$CC) # contingency table

# Chisquare test of homogeneity
(chisq_CC_R<-chisq.test(cc_tab_R))# Table S3


# Observed vs expected counts and residuals
(CC_R_observed_counts <- chisq_CC_R$observed)
CC_R_expected_counts <- chisq_CC_R$expected
print(round(CC_R_expected_counts, 1))
CC_R_pearson_residuals <- chisq_CC_R$residuals
print(round(CC_R_pearson_residuals, 2))

# Calculate contribution to chi-square statistic
CC_R_contributions <- (CC_R_observed_counts - CC_R_expected_counts)^2 / CC_R_expected_counts

# Calculate percentage contributions
CC_R_total_chi_square <- chisq_CC_R$statistic
CC_R_percentage_contributions <- 100 * CC_R_contributions / CC_R_total_chi_square

# Print percentage contributions
print("Percentage Contributions:")
print(round(CC_R_percentage_contributions, 2)) # Table S4
```

### By site
```{r, echo=FALSE}
cc_tab_S <- table(cc_tab$SITE_NAME, cc_tab$CC) # contingency table
(chisq_CC_S<-chisq.test(cc_tab_S))# Table S3

# Observed vs expected counts and residuals
(CC_S_observed_counts <- chisq_CC_S$observed)
CC_S_expected_counts <- chisq_CC_S$expected
print(round(CC_S_expected_counts, 1))
CC_S_pearson_residuals <- chisq_CC_S$residuals
print(round(CC_S_pearson_residuals, 2))

# Calculate contribution to chi-square statistic
CC_S_contributions <- (CC_S_observed_counts - CC_S_expected_counts)^2 / CC_S_expected_counts

# Calculate percentage contributions
CC_S_total_chi_square <- chisq_CC_S$statistic
CC_S_percentage_contributions <- 100 * CC_S_contributions / CC_S_total_chi_square

# Print percentage contributions
print("Percentage Contributions:")
print(round(CC_S_percentage_contributions, 2)) # Table S4
```
